newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico may issue longer-term paper - govt official.
newsitem.headline: Mexico may issue longer-term paper - govt official.

text.p: Mexico could issue two-year Cetes and long-term UDIs, or inflation-linked instruments, by the end of the year, Deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner said on Wednesday.
But he said the government first wanted to see how new private pension funds, known as Afores, operate before introducing the long-term instruments.
"Two-year Cetes could be interesting for the market...," Werner said in a conference call with financial analysts.
He said the government's policy was to extend the maturities of the UDIs very gradually.
At present the longest term Cetes have maturities of one year, while the UDIs have five-year terms.
The Afores, which will begin operating July 1, are expected to increase the market for peso-denominated debt.
Werner also said the government's first priority in managing its external debt was to smooth out its amortization profile. "Where opportunities present themselves, we will take them," he said.
He said one benefit of the government's aggressive debt-rescheduling activities was that it had the option of being much less active in markets in the future.
